answer: Applicants enroll at a mapped reef by drawing one numbered limestone hollow for a full tidal cycle. They leave a wax squeeze of that chamber's unique borings and a 40-minute hydrophone reel, then at culmination sight a listed nebula through a bonded theodolite and stamp the altitude onto the reel. Hollows are issued one per night. Two reels that share a device attestation, a theodolite serial, or an 8-bit exposure prefix forfeit an 85-unit bond, and both serials are retired for a season. One theodolite may graduate only one agent every 18 days.
